newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YOUNG MURRAY OUTDUELS MADDUX AS PADRES BEAT BRAVES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YOUNG MURRAY OUTDUELS MADDUX AS PADRES BEAT BRAVES.

text.p: Untested Heath Murray outdueled the great Greg Maddux to win his first major-league start on Monday as the San Diego Padres beat the National League-leading Atlanta Braves 5-4.
Wally Joyner's RBI double capped a three-run fifth inning off multiple Cy Young winner Maddux that propelled the suddenly hot Padres to their fourth straight victory.

Murray (1-0), a 24-year-old left-hander, gave up four runs and seven hits over 6 1/3 innings. He left with a 5-2 lead in the seventh, but was charged with two more runs when reliever Tim Worrell surrendered a two-run single to Chipper Jones.
"He (Murray) was huge," said San Diego's sweet-swinging Tony Gwynn. "This was a big game for us, they've beaten us five in a row and they haven't even been close."
The Padres, who got off to a bad start this season, improved to 24-30 but remained last in the National League West. Atlanta slipped to 37-18, still the league's best record.

"We'll take any win we can get right now," San Diego slugger Ken Caminiti said. "We've dug ourselves into a hole and we'll get out of it. You see the karma and the attitudes in the clubhouse getting better.
"That was big. He (Murray) pitched a good game, seven good innings, he showed composure and I think he's just going to get better."
Murray worked out of a bases-loaded, no-out jam in the fourth. He struck out Eddie Perez, got Maddux to pop out and fanned Kenny Lofton.
"That inning where we had bases loaded and nobody out came back to haunt us," Chipper Jones said.
Maddux (6-2) had his six-game winning streak snapped as he allowed a season-high five runs and nine hits in seven innings.

In St Louis, red-hot slugger Andres Galarraga drilled a three-run homer in the fifth inning and drove in four runs as the Colorado Rockies built an early lead and held on for an 11-7 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals.
John Burke (1-1) picked up his first win of the season despite allowing five runs and nine hits in five innings as the Rockies claimed their third straight victory.
Danny Jackson (1-1) took the loss.
Galarraga has hit safely in seven straight games, going 14- for-31 (.462) with five homers and 14 RBI.
Ray Lankford went 3-for-3 including his 10th homer and drove in four runs for the Cardinals.

At Florida, Al Leiter tossed seven scoreless innings in his longest start of the season and surging Bobby Bonilla added a pair of hits, including a two-run triple, to pace the Florida Marlins to a 4-2 win over the San Francisco Giants.
Leiter improved to 5-3 as Robb Nen retired Barry Bonds with the tying runs on base in the ninth to notch his 14th save.
The Marlins moved to within 4 1/2 games of the Braves in the East. The Giants' lead over the Rockies in the West shrank to one-half a game.
Bonds was distressed by his failure to come through.

"I take full responsibility," he said. "When Nen came in I was excited that the guys battled back. But it didn't work out and it hasn't since April 1. I passed frustrated a long time ago -- I shouldn't be allowed to wear the uniform."

In Chicago, Terry Mulholland allowed one run and four hits over seven innings and Brant Brown had three hits, including his second home run of the season, as the Chicago Cubs posted their third straight win, 3-2 over the Pittsburgh Pirates.
Mulholland (5-4) walked one and struck out five and Terry Adams pitched the final two innings to record his eighth save.
In New York, Carlos Perez tossed a six-hit shutout and Joe Orsulak burned his former team with a three-run homer as the Montreal Expos routed the Mets 10-0.
Perez (5-4) snapped a personal five-game winless drought by checking the Mets on five singles and a double.

"When I saw all the rain I didn't think I would pitch tonight," said Perez of the 74-minute delay at the start. "I didn't do any of my pre-game stretching and when I found out we were going to play, I didn't have much time to warm up. It's funny, I ended up pitching my best game of the year."
The loss snapped the Mets' four-game winning streak.
In Houston, Donne Wall and Jose Lima combined on a six- hitter and Brad Ausmus had a two-run double in the seventh to lead the Astros to a 2-0 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Wall (2-2) allowed five hits, three walks and tied a career high with nine strikeouts over seven innings.

Houston won with two runs in the seventh off Dodgers starter Hideo Nomo (5-5). Luis Gonzalez led off the inning with a double and Bill Spiers drew a walk. Ausmus followed with a double to deep centre to make it 2-0.
Nomo, who lost his third straight start, yielded six hits and two walks with five strikeouts in six-plus innings.
"We had the same number of hits as they did," said Dodgers manager Bill Russell. "The difference was that they got the big hits and we didn't."
In Philadelphia, the Phillies' game against the Cincinnati Red was postponed due to rain.
